applied.d-logic-home: Mongo backend in the legacy-billing facade: a `backends/mongo.py` module selected by BILLING_BACKEND=mongo; facade.py, app.py and reports.py keep their routes and stop calling the Oracle backend directly.

bd-overdue-status-owner.effect: may add a job or route that sets invoices.statusCd = 40; nobody in the app does today

d-cdc-connector.effect: names who writes the Oracle->Atlas delta after each unit's initial load; no unit's scope depends on it

d-mainframe-load.effect: names the post-cutover loader of invoice_feed / invoice_feed_quarantine; U4 fixes their shape and loads the census rows once, the recurring loader is not in U4

units.name: foundation
scaffolding: backends/mongo.py skeleton behind BILLING_BACKEND=mongo (MONGODB_ATLAS_URI by name, database ow_tp_billing_20261001T233613Z)
mongo:7 fixture container in docker-compose.tp.yml and the tp-golden-smoke legacy-billing job (pymongo added to the uv run deps)

units.name: customers
scaffolding: customer sub-document of GET /api/v1/billing/me (the route stays in U1; U2 fills its `customer` key)

units.name: invoicing

billing_audit_log load + recon (0 live rows); the writer helper itself ships in U1

U5 live recon needs U4's invoices loaded; both wave 2, checked in s4.2.verify
`customer` key is null on the Mongo backend until U2 lands; parity of that key is a wave-2 check
CUSTBILL extract joins customers; both wave 2
reconciliation report groups customers by conversionBatchNo (ix_customers_conversion_batch is owned by U2)
every module appends audit documents outside its transaction; U5 owns the collection's load, recon and retention
